clinician.final_diagnosis: Malignant Peritoneal Mesothelioma (MPM) of epidermoid type
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old woman with history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, pancreatic cysts, and fibromyalgia presented to the emergency department with constitutional syndrome, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. Prior workup including upper and lower endoscopy and serum tumor markers had been normal. During hospitalization, she developed increased abdominal pain, prompting CT imaging of the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis, which revealed peritoneal effusion with signs of peritoneal carcinomatosis (especially in the lesser omentum) and adnexal edema suggesting secondary involvement. A biopsy was subsequently performed that confirmed the diagnosis of mesothelioma (MPM) of epidermoid type. Following diagnosis, she underwent cytoreductive surgery including resection of the round and falciform ligament and omental cake/partial greater omentum resection, combined with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC). Due to extensive disease, she was referred to palliative chemotherapy at her local hospital, which she continues to receive with partial response to treatment.
